short_description.id: Wakwak adalah makhluk mirip burung pengisap darah dalam mitologi Filipina yang konon menyambar manusia pada malam hari; namanya dikaitkan dengan bunyi kepakan sayapnya.
short_description.en: The wakwak is a vampiric, bird-like creature of Philippine mythology said to snatch humans at night; its name is linked to the sound of its flapping wings.

long_description.id: Wakwak adalah makhluk mirip burung pengisap darah dalam mitologi Filipina yang konon menyambar manusia pada malam hari sebagai mangsa, seperti manananggal dan ekek di pedesaan Filipina. Berbeda dari manananggal, ia tidak dapat memisahkan torsonya dari tubuhnya. Sebagian orang meyakininya sejenis vampir, sedangkan yang lain menganggapnya burung malam Filipina yang dikaitkan dengan penyihir.
long_description.en: The wakwak is a vampiric, bird-like creature of Philippine mythology said to snatch humans at night as prey, like the manananggal and the ekek in rural areas of the Philippines. Unlike the manananggal, it cannot separate its torso from its body. Some believe it to be a kind of vampire, while others hold it to be a Philippine night bird associated with witches.

long_description.id: Wakwak sering digambarkan bercakar panjang dan tajam serta bersayap seperti kelelawar; cakar itu dipakai untuk mencabik korban dan mengambil jantungnya. Makhluk ini diyakini dinamai menurut bunyi kepakan sayapnya, yang hanya terdengar saat ia berburu dan makin pelan ketika ia mendekat. Bunyi wakwak biasanya dikaitkan dengan kehadiran Unglu (vampir) atau Ungo (hantu atau monster), dan bunyi tuko pada malam hari pernah pula dikaitkan dengan wakwak.
long_description.en: The wakwak is often described with long sharp talons and bat-like wings, which it uses to slash victims and take their hearts. The creature is believed to be named after the sound of its flapping wings, heard only while it hunts and softer the nearer it comes. The sound is commonly tied to an Unglu (vampire) or Ungo (ghost or monster) being nearby, and a tuko's call at night was once also put down to a wakwak.

long_description.id: Catatan daerah menggambarkannya berbeda-beda. Dalam narasi Aklanon "Encounter with a Wakwak", sang tamu malam mula-mula tampak seperti kelelawar hitam yang amat besar lalu muncul sebagai perempuan berambut panjang, dan tidak ada bagian bawah tubuh yang terlepas. Seorang penulis menuturkan bahwa ibunya di Dulag, Leyte Timur, melihat burung besar kuning kecokelatan bercakar hitam dengan wajah feminin berambut ikal kuning, dan bahwa seorang kerabat ayahnya di Antique melihat wakwak terbang terbalik. Penulis yang sama menyebut bahwa di beberapa daerah Visayas penduduk menamai manananggal dengan wakwak, sedangkan ibunya membedakan keduanya.
long_description.en: Regional records describe it differently. In the Aklanon narrative "Encounter with a Wakwak" the night visitor looks at first like a very large black bat and then turns up as a woman with long hair, and no lower body comes loose. A writer recounts that his mother in Dulag, Eastern Leyte, saw a large tawny bird with black talons and a feminine face with yellow curly hair, and that a relative of his father in Antique saw a wakwak flying upside down. The same writer says that in some areas of the Visayas locals give the name wakwak to the manananggal, while his mother told the two apart.

long_description.id: Sebuah artikel jurnal tentang aswang mencatat bahwa nama seperti wakwak, kiki, atau kaskas di Negros Oriental dan Cebu adalah kata onomatope yang menirukan bunyi, dan bahwa serangan aswang sering didahului bunyi kepakan sayap di atap. Folklorwan Maximo D. Ramos menempatkan wakwak dalam kategori penyedot jeroan, dan catatan tahun 1924 dari Carcar, Cebu, serta koleksi dari Bohol memakai istilah ongo dan wakwak. Dalam catatan dari Bato-bato, ranting jeruk di bawah rumah perempuan hamil dipercaya mencegah wakwak memakannya.
long_description.en: A journal article on the aswang notes that names such as wakwak, kiki or kaskas in Negros Oriental and Cebu are onomatopoeic words imitating sounds, and that aswang attacks are often preceded by the sound of flapping wings on the roof. The folklorist Maximo D. Ramos placed the wakwak in his viscera-sucker category, and a 1924 record from Carcar, Cebu, and a collection from Bohol use the terms ongo and wakwak. In a Bato-bato account, citrus branches under the house of a pregnant woman are believed to keep a wakwak from eating her.

claims.quote: The Wakwak is a vampiric, bird-like creature in Philippine mythology. It is said to snatch humans at night as prey, similar to the manananggal and the Ekek in rural areas of the Philippines. The difference between the Manananggal and the Wakwak is that Wakwak cannot separate its torso from its body while the Manananggal can.

statement.id: Wakwak adalah makhluk mirip burung pengisap darah dalam mitologi Filipina yang konon menyambar manusia pada malam hari sebagai mangsa, seperti manananggal dan ekek di pedesaan Filipina; berbeda dari manananggal, wakwak tidak dapat memisahkan torsonya dari tubuhnya.
statement.en: The wakwak is a vampiric, bird-like creature of Philippine mythology said to snatch humans at night as prey, like the manananggal and the ekek in rural areas of the Philippines; unlike the manananggal, it cannot separate its torso from its body.

claims.quote: It is also believed that this monster is called "Wakwak" due to the sound it makes when it flaps its wings while flying. This sound is only heard when the Wakwak is hunting and becomes softer the closer it becomes.

statement.id: Monster ini dipercaya dinamai wakwak dari bunyi kepakan sayapnya saat terbang; bunyi itu hanya terdengar saat berburu dan makin pelan saat mendekat.
statement.en: This monster is believed named wakwak after the sound of its wings in flight; it is heard only when hunting and grows softer as it approaches.

claims.quote: The Wakwak is often described as having long sharp talons and a pair of wings similar to those of a bat. It uses its talons or claws to slash its victims and to get their heart

statement.id: Wakwak sering digambarkan memiliki cakar panjang yang tajam dan sepasang sayap seperti sayap kelelawar; ia memakai cakarnya untuk mencabik korban dan mengambil jantungnya.
statement.en: The wakwak is often described as having long sharp talons and a pair of wings like those of a bat; it uses its talons or claws to slash its victims and take their hearts.

claims.quote: Some believe that the Wakwak is a type or form of a vampire. Other people contend that a Wakwak is a Philippine night bird associated with witches.

statement.id: Sebagian orang meyakini wakwak sebagai jenis atau wujud vampir; yang lain berpendapat wakwak adalah burung malam Filipina yang dikaitkan dengan penyihir.
statement.en: Some believe the wakwak is a type or form of vampire; others contend it is a Philippine night bird associated with witches.

claims.quote: The sound of a Wakwak (Yaya) is usually associated with the presence of an Unglu (vampire) or Ungo (ghost or monster).

statement.id: Bunyi wakwak (Yaya) biasanya dikaitkan dengan kehadiran Unglu (vampir) atau Ungo (hantu atau monster).
statement.en: The sound of a wakwak (Yaya) is usually associated with the presence of an Unglu (vampire) or Ungo (ghost or monster).

claims.quote: The sound that a tuko (common house gecko) makes at night when out of sight was discovered by an American who spent much time in the Philippines to be attributed to a Wakwak.

statement.id: Bunyi tuko (cicak rumah biasa) pada malam hari ketika tak terlihat ternyata oleh seorang Amerika yang lama tinggal di Filipina dikaitkan dengan wakwak.
statement.en: The sound a tuko (common house gecko) makes at night when out of sight was found by an American who spent much time in the Philippines to be attributed to a wakwak.

claims.quote: the Manananggal and Wakwak are other types of evil creatures in the same league as the Aswang.

statement.id: Manananggal dan wakwak disebut jenis makhluk jahat lain yang sekelas dengan aswang.
statement.en: The manananggal and wakwak are described as other types of evil creatures in the same league as the aswang.

claims.quote: Legend says the Manananggal is a pretty woman by day that transforms into a vicious, half bodied, viscera-eating monster by nightfall. ... In some areas in the Philippines particularly the Visayas, the locals call it the Wakwak. The Wakwak is so named for the sound its wing makes while hovering or flying.

statement.id: Menurut penulis ini, di beberapa daerah, terutama Visayas, penduduk menyebut manananggal (perempuan cantik di siang hari yang berubah menjadi monster pemakan jeroan berbadan separuh pada malam hari) sebagai wakwak, nama yang berasal dari bunyi sayapnya saat melayang atau terbang.
statement.en: According to this writer, in some areas, particularly the Visayas, locals call the manananggal (a pretty woman by day that becomes a half-bodied, viscera-eating monster at night) the wakwak, so named for the sound its wing makes while hovering or flying.

claims.quote: Wakwak, recorded in several Visayan traditions, may name a dangerous night-flying being or imitate its cry.
claims.locator: Manananggal, Wakwak, and Aswang: Why the Names Should Not Be Collapsed

statement.id: Wakwak, yang tercatat dalam beberapa tradisi Visayas, dapat menamai makhluk terbang malam yang berbahaya atau meniru jeritannya.
statement.en: Wakwak, recorded in several Visayan traditions, may name a dangerous night-flying being or imitate its cry.

claims.quote: Maximo D. Ramos, the Filipino folklorist whose comparative studies helped organize a very large body of Philippine material, placed the manananggal and wakwak within his “viscera-sucker” category.
claims.locator: Manananggal, Wakwak, and Aswang: Why the Names Should Not Be Collapsed

statement.id: Folklorwan Maximo D. Ramos menempatkan manananggal dan wakwak dalam kategori "penyedot jeroan" (viscera-sucker) buatannya.
statement.en: The folklorist Maximo D. Ramos placed the manananggal and wakwak within his "viscera-sucker" category.

claims.quote: the Aklanon narrative “Encounter with a Wakwak” describes a night encounter in which the being first resembles an unusually large black bat and then appears as a long-haired woman. The narrator associates it with the repeated cry wak, wak, wak. This account does not describe a detachable lower body

statement.id: Narasi Aklanon "Encounter with a Wakwak" menggambarkan pertemuan malam hari: makhluk itu mula-mula menyerupai kelelawar hitam yang sangat besar lalu tampak sebagai perempuan berambut panjang; penutur mengaitkannya dengan seruan berulang wak, wak, wak, dan kisah itu tidak menyebut bagian bawah tubuh yang dapat terlepas.
statement.en: The Aklanon narrative "Encounter with a Wakwak" describes a night encounter in which the being first resembles an unusually large black bat and then appears as a long-haired woman; the narrator associates it with the repeated cry wak, wak, wak, and the account does not describe a detachable lower body.

claims.quote: Ceferino P. Canaya’s 1924 record from Carcar, Cebu, uses ongo and wakwak. Francisco B. Reyes’s 1924 Bohol collection also records ongo and wakwak

statement.id: Catatan tahun 1924 dari Carcar, Cebu, dan koleksi tahun 1924 dari Bohol sama-sama memakai istilah ongo dan wakwak.
statement.en: A 1924 record from Carcar, Cebu, and a 1924 Bohol collection both use the terms ongo and wakwak.

claims.quote: My Mother’s account of the Wakwak ... my mother has seen one in her teens, out in the rice fields, back in her hometown of Dulag in Eastern Leyte. ... She said she saw what she thought was a large, tawny looking bird with sharp, black talons just a few feet above her head.
claims.locator: My Mother’s account of the Wakwak

statement.id: Seorang penulis menuturkan kisah ibunya, yang di masa remaja di sawah di kota asalnya, Dulag, Leyte Timur, melihat apa yang ia kira burung besar berwarna kuning kecokelatan dengan cakar hitam tajam beberapa kaki di atas kepalanya.
statement.en: A writer recounts his mother's account: in her teens, in the rice fields of her hometown of Dulag in Eastern Leyte, she saw what she thought was a large, tawny bird with sharp black talons a few feet above her head.

claims.quote: She says the thing had a pretty humanoid and feminine face with yellow curly hair. She described its face as looking “like a doll.” Its wings were that of a bird, not a bat.
claims.locator: My Mother’s account of the Wakwak

statement.id: Dalam kisah yang sama, makhluk itu berwajah mirip manusia, cantik dan feminin, berambut ikal kuning, seperti wajah boneka, dan sayapnya sayap burung, bukan kelelawar.
statement.en: In the same account the creature had a pretty humanoid, feminine face with yellow curly hair, like a doll's face, and its wings were a bird's, not a bat's.

claims.quote: In the movies it is normally portrayed as flying in an upright position. My father who grew up in Antique, in the island of Panay, says this is not so. He has a relative who saw a Wakwak flying over a bamboo grove. Dad’s kin says with all lucidity and sobriety that the thing flew upside down.

statement.id: Penulis menyebut film biasanya menggambarkan wakwak terbang tegak, tetapi menurut ayahnya, yang besar di Antique, Pulau Panay, seorang kerabatnya melihat wakwak terbang di atas rumpun bambu dalam posisi terbalik.
statement.en: The writer says films normally portray the wakwak flying upright, but his father, who grew up in Antique on the island of Panay, says a relative saw a wakwak flying over a bamboo grove upside down.

claims.quote: A Bato-bato account recommends placing citrus branches beneath a house where a pregnant woman lives so that a wakwak cannot eat her.

statement.id: Sebuah catatan dari Bato-bato menganjurkan menaruh ranting jeruk di bawah rumah tempat perempuan hamil tinggal agar wakwak tidak dapat memakannya.
statement.en: A Bato-bato account recommends placing citrus branches beneath a house where a pregnant woman lives so that a wakwak cannot eat her.

claims.quote: Tiktik and wakwak ... These names are connected with sounds interpreted as signs of a dangerous nocturnal being. The relationship between sound, bird, and aswang varies by account.

statement.id: Nama tiktik dan wakwak dikaitkan dengan bunyi yang ditafsirkan sebagai tanda makhluk malam yang berbahaya; hubungan antara bunyi, burung, dan aswang berbeda-beda menurut catatan.
statement.en: The names tiktik and wakwak are connected with sounds interpreted as signs of a dangerous nocturnal being; the relationship between sound, bird and aswang varies by account.

claims.quote: Aswang are often heard before they are seen: their attacks are presaged by bird cries emitted either by aswang themselves or their animal familiars (tiktik, kikik), or by the sound of flapping wings on the roof (wakwak or kaskas).

statement.id: Menurut artikel jurnal ini, aswang sering terdengar sebelum terlihat: serangannya didahului pekik burung atau bunyi kepakan sayap di atap (wakwak atau kaskas).
statement.en: According to this journal article, aswang are often heard before they are seen: their attacks are presaged by bird cries or by the sound of flapping wings on the roof (wakwak or kaskas).

claims.quote: Many of the aswang’s names in diverse Philippine ethnolinguistic regions are onomatopoeic words that approximate these noises (tiktik in Aklan, kikik or kakak in Bicol, wakwak, kiki, or kaskas in Negros Oriental and Cebu)

statement.id: Banyak nama aswang di berbagai wilayah etnolinguistik Filipina adalah kata onomatope yang menirukan bunyi itu; wakwak, kiki, atau kaskas dipakai di Negros Oriental dan Cebu.
statement.en: Many names of the aswang in diverse Philippine ethnolinguistic regions are onomatopoeic words approximating these noises; wakwak, kiki or kaskas are used in Negros Oriental and Cebu.
